archetype.name: Lost Season (better than the record)
archetype.definition: A 26-56 year that was over by November, but the margin underneath was clearly healthier than the 21-61 disaster before it, and the forward core played like a real one.

report.headline: Same cellar, firmer floor: forwards worked, the guards and the glass didn't

recap.finish: 26-56, tied with Dallas for third in the Southwest; missed the postseason
recap.body:
New Orleans was effectively a forward-heavy team with no reliable guard play and no defensive rebounding. The sheet lists two coaches, James Borrego and Willie Green, for a season that was decided before it settled. An 0-5 October ran into a 3-13 November, and the team was 3-18 at the end of the month. That hole ended any race before Christmas.

The middle of the year was better than the record suggests. December's 5-9 came with 122.21 points a game, and February's 6-4 was the only winning month, with the Pelicans outscoring opponents on the month. The longest win streak reached five. Even so, the year ended badly: 6-9 in March and 1-5 in April, including a 1-9 final ten games at 10.4 points a game worse than the opponent. A nine-game losing streak sits on the ledger too.

The working parts were up front. Trey Murphy III (10th of 96 on his tab, 61.3 TS %, 214 threes, 6 Win Shares) and Zion Williamson (11th of 93, 64.4 TS %, 6.1 Win Shares in 62 games) were both top-tier at their positions. Saddiq Bey added 5.4 Win Shares, and Karlo Matković shot 69.6 TS % off the bench. The wings graded B- and the frontcourt C+. The offense lived inside and at the line: a 3PA Rate of 35.5 that ranked 26th, offset by a FT Rate ranked 8th, an ORB % ranked 8th and a TOV % ranked 8th. The result was an ORtg of 114.4, 20th and close to league average.

The defense and the backcourt sank it. The DRtg of 118.9 ranked 25th, and the cause wasn't the arc: opponents shot 35% from three, fifth-best in the league. The damage came on second chances and against two positions. The DRB % of 71.4 ranked 28th. Opposing centers averaged 14.29 rebounds a game, and opposing shooting guards scored 32.9 a game, 3.89 above their own averages, the worst mark in the league. The backcourt graded F. Jeremiah Fears played all 82 games at a 25.5 USG % but a 52.5 TS % with a -5 On-Off. Jordan Poole shot 53 TS % at similar usage, and Micah Peavy posted a -5.2 BPM. The four listed guards combined for 2.9 Win Shares.

The record also undersold the team. The point differential implied 30 wins, and the W vs Pt Diff of -4 ranked 27th. That habit is long-running: the club has finished below its margin in four of the previous five seasons. Net Rtg climbed from -9.5 to -4.5, and the site moved it from 28th to 22nd. That is real progress, but not enough to change the outcome.

highlights.title: Murphy and Zion played like stars
highlights.body: Murphy and Williamson both ranked in the top dozen at their positions. Each produced about six Win Shares on efficient scoring, Murphy as a high-volume shooter and Zion as a 64.4 TS % interior force. Bey made it three forwards who carried real loads. This is the part of the roster that already works; the only question is Zion's 62 games.

highlights.title: The margin halved from last year
highlights.body: Net Rtg improved from -9.5 to -4.5. The point differential implied 30 wins, not 26. Some of the gap between the record and the play is close-game luck, which tends to even out. This franchise has run below its margin for years, though, so don't bank all of it.

highlights.title: Possessions protected, extra ones created
highlights.body: Even with few threes, the offense stayed near average by not wasting trips. It ranked 8th in TOV %, 8th in FT Rate and 8th in ORB %. That profile suits a Zion-centered attack and should carry over.

lowlights.title: An F backcourt at high usage
lowlights.body: Fears and Poole used a quarter of the possessions while on the floor and converted them at about 53 TS %. Both had sharply negative On-Off numbers. The listed guards produced 2.9 Win Shares combined against 12.1 from three wings. Unless the guards improve or change, this grade is the ceiling on the whole team.

lowlights.title: The defensive glass kept eroding
lowlights.body: DRB % ranked 28th at 71.4. That continues a slide from 80 five seasons ago, which makes it a trend rather than a blip. Opposing centers feasted on the boards, and Derik Queen's -5.5 On-Off over 2,023 minutes sits alongside it. With the perimeter defense against threes ranked fifth, the 25th-ranked defense is largely a rebounding and interior problem.

lowlights.title: Shooting guards torched it
lowlights.body: Opposing shooting guards scored 32.9 a game, 3.89 over their norms, and both marks ranked last or next to last. That points straight at the weak guard group's defense as well as its offense.

arc.note: The season was buried at 3-18 by the end of November, then partly recovered through a winning February. It collapsed again with a 1-9 close, allowing 126.3 a game.

recap.nextYear: The carryover is the forward trio. Murphy, Williamson and Bey generated most of the team's value, and Matković's efficiency off the bench is a real asset. Williamson's availability, 62 games, is the swing factor. The work is in the backcourt, where the F grade, the guards' high usage on low efficiency and the league-worst defense against shooting guards all point the same way. The other fix is the defensive glass, a six-season slide now ranking 28th. Some of the gap between 26 wins and the 30 the margin implied should come back as close games even out. The team has underrun its differential almost every year, though, so the real gains have to come from fixing those two groups rather than from better luck."

confidence.note: Full 82-game season; the trends line up with five years of history.
